Both Alström syndrome (AS) and maturity-onset diabetes of the young type 1 (MODY1) are linked to nuclear receptor dysfunction. AS is caused by mutations in HNF4A, a key regulator of metabolic genes involved in glucose and lipid homeostasis. Both HNF4A and RARB are nuclear receptors that converge on the broader 'Nuclear receptor signaling pathway', affecting downstream transcriptional programs that regulate cellular differentiation and metabolism, ultimately leading to the distinct phenotypes of AS and MODY1.
